source: Conventions, not law: the emergency-fund target of three months of spending is the low end of the 3–6 months the FOO ladder's step names (data/foo_rules.json); the twelve-month horizon is the same 'over a year' the Rule of Five preset assumes when no date is set. Both are starting points the household can change by changing what it saves.
confidenceNote: A rule of thumb. The right number of months depends on how steady the income is; Variable Income's buffer is the place that reasons about that.
note: Read by engines/presets.js for the Savings presets. Never inline these in a calculator. ruleOfFive is a second convention, read only by the suggestion engine (D-205).

ruleOfFive.label: Rule of 5
ruleOfFive.source: A rule of thumb that circulates in personal-finance writing: keep age ÷ 5 months of spending as a buffer, so a 30-year-old keeps six months and a 50-year-old ten. A convention, not a benchmark; it scales the cushion with the years it takes to rebuild one.
ruleOfFive.note: Read by shared/suggest.js (rule bufferFromAge) to SUGGEST a buffer target; never stored until confirmed. D-205.
